---
title: "Scrape: social platforms"
engine: knitr
---

The "List of most popular social platforms" page has three tables: a 1-row stub, a 5-row table of video-calling apps with a `No.` ranking column, and the 36-row table we actually want. All three share overlapping column names, so instead of matching on a header string we pick the table that has `Country[b]` but not `No.`.

```{python}
#| label: scrape-social
#| eval: false
import io
import pandas as pd
import requests

url = "https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_most_popular_social_platforms"
html = requests.get(url, headers={"User-Agent": "wikimill-project/0.1"}).text

tables = pd.read_html(io.StringIO(html))
social = next(t for t in tables if "Country[b]" in t.columns and "No." not in t.columns)
social.columns = ["name", "company", "country", "launched", "monthly_active_users", "other_metrics"]
social.to_csv("data/social_platforms.csv", index=False)
social.head()
```

This chunk is shown for reference only (`eval: false`), so rendering the site doesn't hit Wikipedia. Run `python src/scrape_social.py` from the project root to refresh `data/social_platforms.csv`. See [clean_social.qmd](clean_social.qmd) for the next step.
